notes: Web 433 — NAV-TRUCK-ROUTING (Nov 12, 2026; layers on web 432). The owner's filmed report, Nov 12 11:12 CST: the Navigator routed him along 48 Avenue NE — in his words a '50% weight legal' (weight-restricted) street — and on the next loaded run over the job-site to dump-site pair it again chose that inside road over the Métis Trail route he had deliberately driven to teach it ('I was just training it last time that it's not supposed to take me from the inside road, it's supposed to take me from Métis. It did not though.'). THREE fixes. (1) LOADED BY DEFAULT: the tandem-dump default profile weight is now the truck's licensed mass — 24.3 t (24,300 kg, its Alberta registration) — so truck costing assumes a LOADED truck; a saved vehicle record still overrides per-field exactly as v356 built it. THE HONEST LIMIT, stated plainly: Calgary's load bans (50/75/90%) exist in NO machine-readable feed (the City publishes a PDF map only; its open truck-route layer carries no load-ban field, and 48 Avenue NE is even listed there as an unrestricted truck route), so no engine can hard-avoid a '50%' street from data. The app therefore SCREENS every adopted truck route (NAVPURE truckNetScreen) against the live City layer plus a driver-reported restriction table (seeded with 48 Avenue NE, '50% weight limit', reported by the owner Nov 12): the reported table is screened first from local data and is never access-exempt; a flagged route is re-asked ONCE with the bad stretch excluded (Valhalla exclude_polygons, inside its 10,000 m circumference cap), and if it still comes back — or the re-ask fails — it is adopted WITH a loud painted + spoken warning ('Weight-restricted street on this route: 48 Avenue NE (50% weight limit) — a loaded truck must not use it. Posted signs govern.'). An empty or failed layer fetch is 'unknown', never a verdict, and never blocks a server route. Off-network/restricted findings keep the bylaw first/last-600 m local-access allowance; reported streets do not. (2) LEARNING NEVER LEARNS A RESTRICTED LEG: every finished drive's trace is screened the same way before it can teach — a flagged drive plants/refreshes/strengthens NOTHING, a flagged drive ON a learned route TAINTS that record (lookup never offers it again), and an unscreenable drive teaches nothing either. (3) THE LEARNED LEGAL ROUTE WINS — AND THE v419 WIRING IS RESTORED: investigation found the web-419 NAV-ML hooks (lookup in doRoute, beginTrip, pushFix, finishTrip, off-route suppression) had been silently dropped by a post-419 ship and stayed dropped through web 432 — js/navlearn.js loaded but nothing called it, which is exactly why his driven Métis route never stood a chance. All hooks are restored; a learned route for the pair is now consulted BEFORE the server, screened, and a clean one is ADOPTED as the presented route — it wins over the engine's shortcut (the pure decision, learnedRouteDecision: flagged -> tainted + server routes; unknown -> server routes this once; clean -> adopt). UNTOUCHED: the standstill judge + camera lock (432), Navigate from pin (430), Documents (431), voice (428), counting, timers. Bench: the new suite tools/nav-truck-routing-v433-test.js (45 checks: loaded default 24.3 t; 48 Ave flags from the reported table despite the layer listing it Unrestricted, warning + sub-cap exclusion ring; reported streets never access-exempt while off-network local access is honoured; the legal corridor screens clean; flagged/unknown drives teach nothing, clean drives still plant, a flagged ride taints; and his exact pair-shape — engine-shortest via 48 Ave flags, his learned Métis line screens clean and the decision is ADOPT) plus the restored stage-1 suite (34/34) and the nav regression set A/B against pristine 432 (navigator-test delta = exactly the two deliberate weight pins, 24 -> 24.3). Live probes Nov 12: at 24.3 t the through pair routes Barlow/McKnight (legal, 2.73 km); the filmed access pair still returns the 1.71 km 48 Ave line (its destination is ON that street — under 433 that route now arrives with the exclusion attempt and, failing a legal alternative, the loud warning instead of silence). VERDICT OWED IN HIS HANDS: his next routed drives — a loaded run over the job/dump pair must present his Métis route, and any route touching 48 Avenue NE must warn loudly. Not claimed until he drives it.
